"Act as an expert Systems Designer and Combat Scripter for 2D UI-driven survival strategy games. I need a comprehensive Game Design Document (GDD) for a menu-based zombie survival game featuring a strict Daily Loop and a Turn-Based Combat System.

Core Design Constraints @COMMENT_BODY@ Rules:
- **Zero Live Action / Animation:** The entire game runs through text logs, UI windows, data tables, and click-based interaction nodes (No real-time character movement or action graphics).
- **Core Setting:** A home shelter (hub) and an interactive location map accessed from the front door.

Core Gameplay Loop @COMMENT_BODY@ Systems:
1. **Day Phase @COMMENT_BODY@ Map Exploration:** 
   - Player clicks the door to view the map (Gym, Park, Playground, City Square) ranked by difficulty.
   - Expeditions lead to text-based encounters and zombie combat nodes.
   - Loot collected automatically transfers to the Home Storage Chest upon return.

2. **Turn-Based Combat System:**
   - When encountering zombies, combat is strictly **turn-based (1-to-1 action exchange)**. 
   - Structure: Player makes one action (e.g., shoot, melee attack, use item) -> Zombie makes one counter-action (e.g., advance, attack, screech).
   - **Ranged Combat @COMMENT_BODY@ Crafting:** Players can craft weapons and bullets in the shelter, allowing them to kill zombies from a distance before they close in for melee range.
   - **Escape Mechanic:** If the player chooses the \"Run/Escape\" action, a percentage-based success check determines if the player flees safely without taking damage.

3. **Night Phase @COMMENT_BODY@ Shelter Upgrades:**
   - Managing home chest inventory.
   - Crafting systems: Food production, ammunition crafting, weapon upgrading, and bag/inventory expansion.

Please structure the design document with the following:
1. **Turn-Based Combat UI @COMMENT_BODY@ Ruleset:** Action economy, distance tracking (ranged vs. melee advantage), and the mathematical formula for the Escape button success rate.
2. **Weapons @COMMENT_BODY@ Ammunition Tree:** Crafting recipes, durability, ammo consumption rates, and range effectiveness against zombies.
3. **Location @COMMENT_BODY@ Loot Progression Table:** Difficulty scaling and drop pools for the Gym, Park, Playground, and City Square.
4. **Shelter @COMMENT_BODY@ Crafting Upgrades:** Detailed upgrade paths for food generation, weapon benches, and inventory bags.

Keep the balance tight, mathematical, and focused on tactical risk management. (2D Game, Phone/Tablet)

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

- Expeditions include encounters/combat; loot automatically transfers to the home chest on return.

Afterlight // design specification

Field manual

Survival is arithmetic. Know what each action costs before you commit.

RULESET 1.0

01 / Turn-based combat

Strict 1-to-1 action exchange: one player action, then one living zombie response. No clocks, animation, or simultaneous actions. Each encounter begins at a location-defined distance. Choose Shoot, Melee, Use item, or Escape.

Shot hit % = clamp(82 − 12×max(0, distance−2) − 15×contact, 20, 92)

Ranged attacks have a 2 m sweet spot. Beyond it, each extra meter lowers accuracy by 12 points. At contact (0 m) accuracy is additionally reduced by 15. A miss consumes one round; a hit deals weapon damage. Zombie advances 1 m if out of reach, otherwise attacks. Every third round it may screech: no damage, but next escape chance −10 points.

Escape % = clamp(65 + 7×distance − 8×threat − 10×wound − 10×screech, 15, 90)

Threat = route tier modifier (0–3); wound = 1 below 50% health; screech = 1 while rattled. Successful escape secures the field bag and ends the outing. Defeat recovers half the bag, rounded down.

02 / Weapons & ammunition tree

  • Pipe: 7 damage, 0 ammo, durability 12 hits. Craft: 2 scrap + 1 wood.
  • Revolver: 12 damage, durability 20 shots. Bench I: 4 scrap + 2 parts; one .38 round per shot.
  • Carbine: 18 damage, durability 24 shots. Bench II: 6 scrap + 4 parts; one 5.56 round per shot.
  • .38 ammunition: craft 4 rounds: 1 scrap + 1 parts. 5.56: craft 3 rounds: 2 scrap + 1 parts.
  • Weapon wear accrues only on successful hits. At 0 durability it is unusable; repair costs 2 scrap + 1 parts for up to 10 durability.

## Objective
- Complete a playable, mobile-friendly, menu-based zombie survival game with a strict daily loop, turn-based combat, shelter upgrades, crafting, and an accurate in-game field manual.

## Requirements
- No live action or animation; gameplay uses text, UI, data, and click/touch interactions.
- Include shelter hub and front-door map with Playground, Park, Gym, and City Square; expeditions, combat, and automatic loot transfer to the home chest.
- Combat exchanges exactly one player action for one zombie counter-action; include ranged/melee, distance, crafted weapons/ammunition, and percentage-based escape.
- Night phase includes chest management, food production, ammunition, weapon upgrades, and bag upgrades.
- Include accurate combat formulas, weapon/ammunition crafting tree, location progression/drop pools, and detailed shelter upgrades.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; state assumptions briefly at completion.
- Save and inspect a small JPEG screenshot at viewport width ≤1280px, reading only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Single-file HTML/CSS/JavaScript game in `index.html`, with localStorage saves.
- Fictional progression starts at Playground; routes unlock on days 2–4; higher tiers increase enemy, loot, and escape risks.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the responsive UI, gameplay, persistence, route/combat/crafting/upgrades, and field manual in `index.html`.
- Fixed malformed HTML nesting; all six views now sit directly inside `.main-card`.
- Verified route entry, failed escape and zombie response, successful escape, loot return, night crafting/upgrades, dawn transition, and localStorage persistence in Chromium.
- Verified mobile map interaction at 390px with no horizontal overflow; JavaScript syntax passes and browser reported no page errors.
- Updated manual route and shelter sections to match implemented pools, drops, costs, effects, and food/health values.
- Updated manual screech wording to match the response-round counter behavior.

### Active
- Test victory, defeat, secure loot transfer, and daily-loop outcomes; recent Playwright attempts did not complete because of hidden-view and ambiguous-selector errors.
- Rerun JavaScript syntax validation with a working extraction command.
- Recapture and inspect the latest ≤1280px JPEG; `/tmp/opencode/afterlight.jpg` predates the recent manual updates.

- (none)

1. Continue browser checks using visible-view navigation and disambiguated selectors; verify victory, defeat, escape, and dawn upkeep/unlocks.
2. Run syntax validation with a temporary JavaScript file or another command that avoids the failed process-substitution approach.
3. Capture a fresh JPEG at 1200×900, read and inspect only that latest screenshot, then report results and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: game UI, gameplay logic, and field manual.
- `/tmp/opencode/afterlight.jpg`: older screenshot; replace and inspect after current manual changes.

## Important Context
- Current implementation gives each route one infected and exactly `2 + threat` initial loot items drawn uniformly from its route pool; victory adds route-specific bonus loot.
